REFERENCE INPUT ROLES:
Image 1, the supplied original: content/mood guidance only for a pale-haired focal adult against darkness and Mial's subjective pink/violet impression. Do NOT copy its anime/digital rendering, crowd, blinding face, bodily glow or public aura.
Images 2 and 3, the actual gallery landscape paintings: PRIMARY references for Canadian Group of Seven inspired oil construction and lighting. Borrow broad interlocking colour/value masses, varied directional opaque bristle strokes, quiet connecting passages, selective substantial impasto, matte pigment and connected restrained shadow shapes. Do not copy their trees, terrain, geography, bright daytime light or palette literally.

SUBJECT: Auvet is ONE adult woman about thirty, clearly the same identity in every study. Pale hair with the left side cut a little shorter in a hurry, in a practical loose braid or gathered length. Distinctive single notch near the outer end of ONE eyebrow, consistently on the same anatomical side in all facial views. Faint asymmetric crease from nose toward one mouth corner, deepening when she begins to smile. A definite individual face, human ordinary proportions and anatomy, alert and slightly impatient but warm. Plain dark, worn coat with carefully mended cuff and modestly frayed lower edge, practical boots. No glamour costume, jewelry, stage regalia, weapon or invented marks.

LAYOUT: a dominant uncropped standing front three-quarter full-body study showing the coat, hands, boots and coherent proportions; a smaller uncropped rear/side full-body view of the same woman showing uneven pale hair, dark coat and mended cuff; and one useful enlarged face detail showing the eyebrow notch and asymmetric mouth crease. Separate views with generous ivory breathing space. If space allows, place one small insubstantial three-step horse shape of red, blue and green light just above her raised fingertips, with a few modest colored reflections only on her fingers/cuff. The tiny colored-light figure is the actual public art she draws and evaporates when her fingers lower; it is not a second character.

PAINT AND LIGHT: paint figure anatomy, face and fabric as decisively simplified coherent oil shapes, not a smooth digital figure with an impasto filter. Story time is evening at a portrait stall: modest warm oil-lamp illumination from one side of the principal view, subdued cool ambient market night in the shadows, believable tonal falloff and lost edges; no street or stall illustrated. Character stays readable, but shadows remain connected and restrained, not studio fill. The colored horse can cast only a little local light. Her huge gold-white inner radiance with pink/violet edge is visible only to Mial's Sprite Eye and must NOT be painted as a literal halo, blazing body, public aura, flames or theatrical rim. The original's pink/violet may inform a tiny low-contrast subjective accent or the small magic figure; do not flood the sheet.

STRICT: exactly one human identity; no other person, crowd, setting, location vignette, floor/terrain patch, decorative splash backdrop, sunlight, glossy or photographic/3D face, anime linework, uniformly bevel-lit paint chips, glossy eyes, cinematic contour lighting or automatic orange/blue split. Clear anatomy in every repeated view.
